newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to raise 3 trln rbls from debts to Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Russia to raise 3 trln rbls from debts to Moscow.

text.p: Russia plans to raise between two to three trillion roubles this year by selling some of the foreign debt owed to Moscow, First Deputy Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin said on Wednesday.

"Part of the measures (to increase budget revenues) will be connected to the sales of some debts to us or their better management," Kudrin told a news conference. "We are planning more talks with countries which either do not pay, or do not pay in full."

Russia, which inherited responsibility for both the assets and the liabilities of the former Soviet Union, is owed about $132 billion, calculated at the former State Soviet Bank rate of about 0.60 roubles per dollar.
It currently receives $1-2 billion annual in debt repayment, half of it in goods.
Russia plans securitising some of the debt as one way to raise repayment.

Russia is facing a severe financial crisis, which is forcing the government to cut planned spending by 105 trillion roubles this year. Domestic tax revenues in the first quarter of thie year were only 49 percent of budgeted levels.
